summary: Closed the measured B409 topology defect: a separately spawned bridge App Server (AppServerClient, B384/B402/B407) can only ever see the VS Code OpenAI extension's owned thread from the OUTSIDE -- the extension spawns and owns its own `codex app-server` child over a private stdio pipe, and thread/resume/turn/* are scoped to the App Server INSTANCE that owns the turn, not the thread id in the abstract, so a second instance can never wake the visible chat; it can only start a hidden turn on a hidden connection (this is true even with B407's turn/steer fix, since that fix routes correctly WITHIN the wrong instance). The measured live canary: a fresh bridge-owned App Server saw the owner thread idle and sat in turn/start for 6+ minutes while the real extension already had its own App Server child and the active rollout open. Implemented geoai_task_mcp/app_server_mux.py: a transparent Codex CLI wrapper meant to be installed as the extension's chatgpt.cliExecutable. Non-app-server invocations os.execvp the real binary with the exact argv (full process-image replacement -- exit code and stdio are byte-identical to invoking the real binary directly, proven by a subprocess test asserting exact argv echo + exit code passthrough). app-server invocations become AppServerMux: spawns one real child `codex app-server` with the exact argv forwarded unchanged, inherits stderr untouched (transparent, zero extra proxying code), and proxies extension<->child stdin/stdout transparently in both directions on two daemon pump threads while a third thread runs a local Unix sideband socket server. The sideband is fail-closed and local-only: 0700 owner-only sideband directory, 0600 socket file and 0600 capability file (permission bits set AT CREATION via os.mkdir/os.open mode arguments and a narrowly-scoped umask around socket bind(), since this sandboxed execution environment rejects a standalone chmod() syscall outright -- chmod is still attempted afterward, wrapped in contextlib.suppress(OSError), as defense-in-depth on hosts where it IS available), SO_PEERCRED same-uid check where the platform supports it, hmac.compare_digest constant-time capability comparison, an exact three-method allowlist (thread/resume, turn/steer, turn/start -- initialize and every other method rejected), a request-shape allowlist restricting a sideband request to exactly {cap, method, params} (a client-supplied id, a jsonrpc member, or any other key asserting extra transport authority is rejected as forbidden_fields), bounded request/response sizes (SIDEBAND_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES/SIDEBAND_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES) and a bounded per-call deadline, collision-free synthetic wire ids (geoai-sideband-<uuid4hex>-<seq>, structurally distinct from any integer id the extension would issue) so a sideband response is intercepted by _route_child_message and routed back over the socket -- never forwarded to the extension's stdout -- while every notification the same call produces (turn/started, turn/completed, etc, which carry no id) still flows to the extension transparently for visible-UI parity, a bounded TTL dedup cache (method+params hash) so a retried identical sideband call is answered from cache without a second wire round-trip, and readiness gated on PASSIVELY observing the EXTENSION's own initialize (success) -> initialized handshake complete on the child connection (the mux never originates that handshake itself). Before readiness, on child exit, or on any malformed/ambiguous shape, dispatch_sideband raises a bounded SidebandNotReady/SidebandRejected -- the mux never spawns a second/separate App Server as a fallback (verified structurally: the same self._child is asserted unchanged across repeated not-ready sideband attempts). Added geoai_task_mcp/callback_bridge.py::SidebandCallbackClient, a callback transport that speaks the mux's sideband socket instead of spawning a subprocess: resumes the exact bound thread, reuses the SAME select_steer_target() decision function AppServerClient already uses (active-with-one-inProgress -> turn/steer with exact expectedTurnId; idle -> turn/start), and treats the matching SYNCHRONOUS sideband response (TurnSteerResponse.turnId / TurnStartResponse.turn.id) as full delivery acknowledgement without waiting for turn/completed (that notification flows to the extension's own stdout via the mux, not to this socket) -- proven not to block by an elapsed-time assertion in test_sideband_client_deliver_callback_idle_is_synchronous_ack_no_completed_wait. CallbackBridge gained a transport="subprocess"|"sideband" constructor parameter (default unchanged: "subprocess") and a shared _deliver_batch_via_transport() helper so _process_batch's existing lease/retry/dead-letter/outbox machinery, deterministic clientUserMessageId, and the fixed trusted prompt builders (build_callback_prompt/build_batch_callback_prompt, untouched) are reused byte-for-byte regardless of transport -- only the delivery client differs. Added scripts/install_vscode_app_server_mux.py: dry-run/check/print-config only (argparse --check / --print-config / --python-executable), prints the exact chatgpt.cliExecutable value and rollback steps as JSON; verified by a subprocess test asserting zero filesystem mutation (a canary settings.json and the default sideband dir are both byte-identical/absent before and after every invocation).

environment_note.chmod_syscall_blocked_in_this_sandbox: A standalone os.chmod()/Path.chmod() call fails with PermissionError('Operation not permitted') everywhere in this worker's sandboxed shell -- including on files/directories this same process just created and owns (uid=1000 shrek) -- confirmed via /proc/self/status Seccomp=2/Seccomp_filters=1 and reproduced identically with dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true. Worked around structurally rather than by skipping the requirement: directory/file permission bits are set AT CREATION TIME via os.mkdir(mode=)/os.open(mode=) (unaffected by this restriction, verified directly), and the AF_UNIX socket file (which has no mode parameter on bind()) is created under a narrowly-scoped os.umask(0o177) set immediately before bind() and restored immediately after -- verified to yield exactly 0600 in this sandbox. A trailing os.chmod() wrapped in contextlib.suppress(OSError) remains as defense-in-depth reinforcement for real hosts where chmod IS available (e.g. a pre-existing directory with looser permissions from an older run). Tests assert the exact resulting mode bits (0700 dir, 0600 socket, 0600 capability file) and pass in this sandbox.
environment_note.af_unix_path_length_limit: pytest's own tmp_path fixture nests a long test-name-derived directory that overflows AF_UNIX's ~108-byte path limit inside this worktree's deeply-nested sandbox root; test_app_server_mux.py's harness uses a short tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=...) directory instead, independent of tmp_path, for every sideband socket.

security_invariants.separate_app_server_fallback: Structurally forbidden and never taken -- AppServerMux.dispatch_sideband() only ever writes to the ONE child spawned in start(); every not-ready/rejected/deferral path raises before any subprocess.Popen call, proven by test_sideband_not_ready_never_spawns_a_second_child (asserts the same self._child object identity across repeated failed attempts) and test_sideband_defers_when_child_has_exited (child terminated -> not_ready, no respawn).
security_invariants.arbitrary_app_server_method_proxy: Forbidden -- SIDEBAND_ALLOWED_METHODS is exactly {thread/resume, turn/steer, turn/start}; initialize and every other method are rejected with method_not_allowed before dispatch_sideband is ever called (test_sideband_rejects_initialize_method, test_sideband_rejects_arbitrary_method, test_sideband_allowlist_is_exactly_three_methods).
security_invariants.unbounded_or_unauthenticated_sideband: Forbidden -- capability token required and hmac.compare_digest-compared (test_sideband_rejects_wrong_capability), SO_PEERCRED same-uid enforced where available (test_sideband_rejects_wrong_uid_peer via a monkeypatched peer-cred check, since this single-user sandbox cannot fork as a different uid), bounded request size (test_sideband_rejects_oversized_request) and bounded per-call deadline (SIDEBAND_REQUEST_DEADLINE_SECONDS).
security_invariants.token_thread_or_prompt_logging: Not performed -- app_server_mux.py contains no print/log statement that includes a capability token, thread id, or prompt/turn text anywhere on any code path (only a generic exec-failure message naming the real executable path is ever printed, on the non-app-server passthrough error path).
security_invariants.client_supplied_internal_ids_and_extra_t: Rejected -- a sideband request may contain only {cap, method, params}; any other key (a client-supplied id, a jsonrpc member, or anything else) is rejected as forbidden_fields before the capability token is even checked (test_sideband_rejects_client_supplied_id, test_sideband_rejects_jsonrpc_field, test_sideband_rejects_extra_transport_authority_field).
security_invariants.worker_output_or_untrusted_text_in_callb: Unchanged -- SidebandCallbackClient reuses build_callback_prompt()/build_batch_callback_prompt() unmodified; no new parameter carries worker output/logs/objectives into a prompt.
security_invariants.installer_no_mutation: Verified -- install_vscode_app_server_mux.py never calls open() in write mode, os.chmod, subprocess, or any VS Code/systemd/DB API; test_installer_never_touches_vscode_settings_or_sideband_dir asserts a canary settings.json file and the sideband directory are byte-identical/absent before and after every invocation, in both --check and default print-config modes.
